paras: The Tryon manhunt of 1903 was an armed search for a Black man near Tryon, Polk County, North Carolina, in February 1903, after he was accused of raping and beating an 18-year-old white girl. Searchers fired on a man they took for the culprit, and the papers reported that he would be lynched if caught. Four days later officers at Forest City arrested Solon Jackson, who denied the assault, and held him for the county authorities.

According to dispatches from Spartanburg and Asheville, a Black man assaulted Nellie Carlisle about 10 o'clock on Sunday morning, February 8, in woods about two miles from Tryon. He was said to have beaten her about the head with rocks and left her apparently dead; she was found hours later and carried home in critical condition. A later telephone report from Polk County said she had been on her way to the home of Lewis Scoggins.

The people of Tryon organized a party that searched for the man without success. Later, at night, several persons saw a Black man trying to board a Southern Railway train at Tryon and opened fire, but he escaped; it was thought he was the man wanted. A special from Tryon to the Charleston Evening Post said that "a band of mountaineers armed with rifles" was scouring the mountains and that a lynching would follow his capture.

On February 12 Constable J. C. Harrill and Chief Jones captured Solon Jackson at Forest City as the "supposed" assailant. Jackson said he had been at his father's in Polk County until Monday afternoon but knew nothing about the assault. The dispatch added that he was just out of the Henderson chain gang.

Jackson was held for the Polk County authorities, and the girl was still reported in critical condition. No report of his transfer, an indictment, a trial or any mob action against him was found, nor of whether the girl recovered.

The story ran only in white papers, among them the Alexandria Gazette, the Savannah Morning News, the Lancaster Ledger and the Richmond Times-Dispatch, between February 10 and 13. The first briefs, headed "Brutal Assault," "Girl Ravished Near Tryon" and "Prospect of a Lynching," called the accused "a negro brute" and "the fiend" and reported without comment that he would be "strung up without ceremony." The Spartanburg account, credited to The State, was reprinted in South Carolina weeklies, while the Raleigh News and Observer carried its own Asheville special headed "Assaulted and Left for Dead."

Once a suspect was in jail, the tone of the follow-up shifted: the News and Observer called Jackson the "supposed" assailant and printed his denial, and the Richmond Times-Dispatch headed the same dispatch "Charged With Assault." No Black-press report of the episode was found.

The girl was named Nellie Carlisle in the first reports and Minnie Carlyle in the Rutherfordton dispatch. A Columbia brief dated February 10 placed the assault "yesterday," February 9, but three other dispatches put it on Sunday, February 8, and the brief appears to restate the earlier Spartanburg report.

reader.title: Tryon manhunt of 1903
bases: After a Black man was accused of assaulting a white girl, armed searchers hunted him, fired on a man thought to be him, and were said to intend lynching him if caught (A1, A3, A6); no killing was reported and the accused was later jailed by officers (A5).

A group of armed men hunted the accused and fired on a suspect under the pretext of punishing an assault, but no one was reported killed (A1, A3, A6); Solon Jackson was arrested by officers and held for the county authorities (A5, A7).
Separate dispatches from Spartanburg, Asheville, Tryon (via Charleston) and Rutherfordton agree on the assault accusation, the armed search and the lynching threat (A1, A3, A5, A6).

accounts.label: Spartanburg dispatch (The State)
accounts.gist: A Black man assaulted Nellie Carlisle on Sunday morning, beat her with rocks and escaped; a search failed, persons fired on a man boarding a train at Tryon, and he would be 'strung up without ceremony' if caught.

accounts.label: Asheville special
accounts.gist: Same sequence, with the assault 'about 10 o'clock Sunday morning' and the gunfire at the train 'last night'.

accounts.label: Tryon special via Charleston
accounts.gist: Armed mountaineers were scouring the mountains and a lynching would follow capture.

accounts.label: Rutherfordton dispatch
accounts.gist: Solon Jackson, the 'supposed' assailant, was captured by officers at Forest City and held for Polk county; he denied the assault.

accounts.label: Accused's statement
accounts.gist: Jackson admitted being at his father's in Polk, leaving Monday afternoon, but said he knew nothing about the assault.

framing.detail: Wire briefs headed 'Brutal Assault' and 'Prospect of a Lynching' call the accused 'a negro brute' and 'the fiend' and report the lynching threat as a matter of course, without comment.
The Raleigh News and Observer's follow-up called Jackson the 'supposed' assailant and printed his denial; the Richmond Times-Dispatch headed it 'Charged With Assault'.

versions.value: Sunday, Feb. 8 ('yesterday morning' in a Feb. 9 dispatch; 'Sunday')
'yesterday' in a dispatch dated Feb. 10, i.e. Feb. 9

conflicts.note: Three independent dispatches put it on Sunday; the Columbia brief appears to restate the Spartanburg dispatch a day later without adjusting 'yesterday'.
A7 prints the same dispatch as A5, which says eighteen; A7's figure is likely a typesetting error.
